questions: Did all of this start suddenly, or did symptoms develop gradually over days to weeks?
Before all this happened, were you completely healthy with no medical problems?
Did something happen to cause this, like an accident or injury?
Was your tracheostomy placed because you had difficulty breathing on your own for a prolonged period?
Before this hospitalization, did you notice any drooping of your eyelids or double vision?
Before this happened, did you notice any weakness in your arms or legs?
Have you been losing weight over the past several months?
Before this hospitalization, did you have difficulty swallowing or choking on food?
Were you previously unable to come off a ventilator after being intubated, which is why the tracheostomy was placed?
Is the eye patch over your right eye because of an injury, or to manage drooping/visual symptoms?
Have you had any previous hospitalizations or surgeries for similar problems?
Are you experiencing any pain right now?
Did your symptoms tend to get worse with activity and improve with rest?
Do you have trouble speaking clearly or with a weak voice?
Have you had any problems with your breathing getting weak, especially later in the day?

results: 1. Complete bedside neurological examination including cranial nerve testing, motor strength, reflexes, and coordination
mental status / cognitive screen: minimally conscious; impaired cognition
muscle tone examination: increased tone; Ashworth grade 1+ upper limbs and grade 2 lower limbs after treatment
limb strength (MRC) examination: not reliably testable because of impaired consciousness and myoclonus
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: brisk deep tendon reflexes; extensor plantar responses
coordination examination (limb and truncal): not testable
posture and pull test: abnormal posture; pull test not testable
MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: restricted diffusion consistent with hypoxic-ischaemic injury
3. CT angiogram of head and neck
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
EEG: diffuse encephalopathic changes without periodic sharp wave complexes
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
